Independent rational admissible constant example K=3,m=1,r=1,p=s=1,a=1,b=1/10,c=2/5,x=2,y=3/10: H1=32/75>0 and H2=111/1000>0 yield a genuine positive constant T-periodic equilibrium, so theorem is not inherently vacuous.

Endpoint conditions x>=0 and 0<m<K checked: production G negative outside (m,K) except zeros, giving global maximum. Source files and all frozen blobs accounted for by independent Git tree SHA construction.
correctness.rationale: Directly reconstruct q=s/p and Phi=x+q y: the Holling-III term s x²/(x²+a²)y cancels against q p x²/(x²+a²)y exactly; the product-rule term is +qdot*y, so Phi_dot=G-H1-qH2-q b y²-(q c-qdot)y. A T-periodic Phi has mean derivative 0. For every u>=0 and 0<m<K the cubic G has unique positive global maximum at u*=(K+m+sqrt(K²-Km+m²))/3; equality in the harvest-only ceiling is impossible for any strictly positive periodic solution because q b y²>0 and eta y>=0. Theta=min qb>0 and eta_L=min eta>=0 together with Jensen yield theta (mean y)^2+eta_L mean y<=Delta; solving gives the stated quadratic-root bound. Hypotheses and quantifiers, including strictly positive cycles only, are consistently stated.
residual_risks: Only a necessary condition for positive T-periodic solutions; no existence or sufficiency, no blanket trapping of all forward solutions, and no conclusion when qc-qdot<0.
Predator mean root is an upper bound using coefficient minima; neither its sharpness nor attainability is proved.
No universal stability threshold, and no conclusion for nonpositive u or different Allee regimes.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge narrowly scoped PASS for the particular source-vector-field periodic formula and joint-harvest/mean-predator conclusions. The classical weighted biomass cancellation and absolute maximum production bound ARE prior methods; they are NOT claimed as novel. The exact Yu–Liu–Lin theorem addresses multiple positive-cycle existence and does not state the necessary variable-conversion-ratio q=s/p weighted budget. Etoua–Rousseau has a weaker autonomous prey-only-harvest structural predecessor and Wang 2020 exhibits the classical analogous weighted-total-population technique. No inspected prior theorem with assumptions that dominate periodic positive coefficients, differentiable q, Allee factor, dual harvesting, predator competition and eta=qc-qdot>=0 was shown to entail all three submitted statements. A same-source theorem may still be an unindexed consequence of standard bioeconomic energy-budget theory; no exhaustive priority certification.
residual_risks: Weighted biomass/trophic energy-budget cancellations are classical; a prior abstract theorem may state a genuinely dominating time-variable conversion formula under another name.

A source-specific necessary harvest condition may be implicit to specialists as an elementary observation even if not printed as a separate theorem; best-of-knowledge PASS is not a priority certificate.

Etoua–Rousseau 2010 Remark 8.2(2) establishes the classic separate prey MSY, whereas the submitted model explicitly harvests both species.

Exact inequivalent harvest ceilings at K=3,m=1,r=1,m=1: Gmax=(20+14 sqrt(7))/81≈0.7042, H1=1/5<Gmax, H1+qH2=4/5>Gmax; this parameter example is used only to demonstrate strength of the necessary bound, not to assert existence.
Specific additional mean predator upper bound from natural nonnegative dissipation terms qb y² and eta y.
value.rationale: A source-motivated and mathematically useful necessary nonexistence test: the original Yu–Liu–Lin paper establishes positive-cycle existence regimes but does not give a combined prey-and-predator harvest obstruction. The proven joint-harvest inequality is strictly stronger than the immediate prey-only bound for positive H2 and remains checkable for arbitrarily varying positive periodic coefficients with qdot compensated by mortality. The nontriviality is demonstrated by K=3,m=1,r=1,q=1,H1=1/5,H2=3/5: H1 lies below the exact maximal G=(20+14 sqrt(7))/81, but H1+q H2=4/5 exceeds it, so the new test excludes locked cycles although prey-only MSY does not. The explicit predator-mean root adds genuinely quantitative control. These are narrow, motivated harvest-management quantities, not arbitrary parameter slices, despite a short elementary proof; neither novel weighted cancellation in general nor global sharpness is asserted.
residual_risks: The derivation uses standard biomass-weighting, elementary polynomial optimization and Jensen; value is modest and source-specific rather than an unprecedented general dynamical method.
The necessary ceiling and predator-mean estimate are not proved globally sharp or sufficient for cycles.
Biological parameter interpretations require care when constant-rate harvesting makes the positive cone non-invariant; theorem quantifies only strictly positive periodic solutions.
